university.name: Imperial College London
university.summary: A London university with its main campus in South Kensington, teaching science, technology, engineering, medicine and business. It admits international students to undergraduate and postgraduate taught programmes, and runs a separate Business School with its own application rounds and scholarships.

courses.title: Finance
courses.duration_text: 12 months full-time (optional 16 month extended term with a work placement)
courses.overview: A one-year Imperial Business School Masters for quantitative graduates, covering corporate finance, derivatives, financial econometrics and portfolio management. An optional extended term adds a four to six month work placement for an additional fee.
courses.academic_requirements: Preferably a First Class Honours degree from a recognised university; an Upper Second Class Honours degree or international equivalent is also considered. Degree subject should be highly quantitative, for example mathematics, engineering, economics, finance or science.
courses.english_requirements: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall, at least 6.5 in every element. TOEFL iBT 100 overall with at least 22 in each element (tests before 21 January 2026) or 5.0 overall with at least 5.0 in each element (tests after that date). Duolingo English Test 125 overall, no band below 115. PTE Academic is not stated on the Business School pages.
courses.experience_requirements: No minimum work experience stated; relevant internships and placements are strongly recommended.
courses.pakistan_entry_note: Imperial accepted qualifications page for postgraduate study: a four year Bachelor's degree awarded from 2016 onwards by a university funded by the Higher Education Commission, with a final overall mark of 75% or better; selectors may ask for a higher mark from some institutions. Older Bachelor's degrees normally also need a Master's.
courses.career_notes: The 2026 entry course page names investment banking, asset and investment management, and sales and trading as options.
courses.application_deadline_note: Round 2 closes 6 January 2027, round 3 on 10 March 2027, round 4 on 28 April 2027 (round 1 closed 29 September 2026).
courses.notes: Fee GBP 54,000 is shown for 2027 entry on the Business School page (total for the 12 month programme); the Imperial study page for 2026 entry showed GBP 51,000 for 12 months. Modules and career line are from the 2026 entry study page: https://www.imperial.ac.uk/study/courses/postgraduate-taught/finance/. The 75% Pakistan figure is a general postgraduate minimum, not specific to this course.

courses.title: Management (MiM)
courses.overview: A one-year Imperial Business School Masters giving a broad grounding in business for graduates of any discipline. The page describes applied learning with academic rigour, preparing students for careers in finance, consulting and innovation.
courses.academic_requirements: A first or upper second-class undergraduate degree (or international equivalent) in any discipline. Candidates are expected to have a basic level of mathematics.
courses.english_requirements: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall, at least 6.5 in every element. TOEFL iBT 100 overall with at least 22 in each element (tests before 21 January 2026) or 5.0 overall with at least 5.0 in each element (tests after that date). Duolingo English Test 125 overall, no band below 115. PTE Academic is not stated on the Business School pages.
courses.experience_requirements: No work experience requirement; experience can strengthen an application but cannot replace the academic requirement.
courses.pakistan_entry_note: Imperial accepted qualifications page for postgraduate study: a four year Bachelor's degree awarded from 2016 onwards by a university funded by the Higher Education Commission, with a final overall mark of 75% or better; selectors may ask for a higher mark from some institutions. Older Bachelor's degrees normally also need a Master's.
courses.career_notes: The page reports that 94% of graduates (combined MSc International Management and MSc Management, Class of 2025) accepted an offer within six months of graduation.
courses.application_deadline_note: Round 2 closes 6 January 2027, round 3 on 10 March 2027, round 4 on 28 April 2027 (round 1 closed 29 September 2026).
courses.notes: Fee is stated as the same for UK and international students, with a GBP 7,000 deposit included. The 75% Pakistan figure is a general postgraduate minimum, not specific to this course.

courses.title: Business Analytics and AI
courses.overview: A one-year Imperial Business School Masters in data-driven decision making, with training in predictive, prescriptive and AI-based decision models. It targets graduates with a quantitative background, including calculus, probability, statistics and linear algebra.
courses.academic_requirements: First or Upper Second Class Honours (or international equivalent) in a quantitative subject such as Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Statistics, Physics or quantitative economics, with advanced calculus, probability, statistics and linear algebra. GMAT or GRE not required.
courses.english_requirements: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall, at least 6.5 in every element. TOEFL iBT 100 overall with at least 22 in each section (tests before 21 January 2026) or 5.0 overall with at least 5.0 in each element (tests after that date). Duolingo English Test 125 overall, no band below 115. PTE Academic is not stated.
courses.experience_requirements: Not required; candidates typically have no more than three years of work experience.
courses.pakistan_entry_note: Imperial accepted qualifications page for postgraduate study: a four year Bachelor's degree awarded from 2016 onwards by a university funded by the Higher Education Commission, with a final overall mark of 75% or better; selectors may ask for a higher mark from some institutions. Older Bachelor's degrees normally also need a Master's.
courses.career_notes: Class of 2025 figures on the page: 97% accepted an offer within six months of graduation, 35% in finance and 22% in technology.
courses.application_deadline_note: Round 2 closes 6 January 2027, round 3 on 10 March 2027, round 4 on 28 April 2027 (round 1 closed 29 September 2026).
courses.notes: The programme page does not explicitly tie the GBP 51,000 fee to an academic year; it appears beside the 2027 intake. The 75% Pakistan figure is a general postgraduate minimum, not specific to this course.

courses.title: Computing
courses.overview: A one-year conversion Masters for graduates from non-computing backgrounds, covering programming principles, computer systems and modern software technologies, followed by electives and an individual research project with a dissertation and oral presentation.
highlights: Organisation and operation of a computer system
courses.academic_requirements: First-Class degree in a subject without substantial Computing content. The Department of Computing page adds that non-STEM applicants need at least an A in A-level Mathematics (or equivalent) and must submit those results.
courses.english_requirements: Not stated on the course page or the Department of Computing page. Imperial's English language page lists a standard level (IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, 6.0 in every element) and a higher level (7.0 overall, 6.5 in every element) and says course pages state which applies; this one does not.
courses.pakistan_entry_note: Imperial accepted qualifications page for postgraduate study: a four year Bachelor's degree awarded from 2016 onwards by a university funded by the Higher Education Commission, with a final overall mark of 75% or better; selectors may ask for a higher mark from some institutions. Older Bachelor's degrees normally also need a Master's.
courses.career_notes: The page lists roles in application and web development, networking and AI, with other paths in chip design, cyber security, data management, biomedical systems and transport.
courses.application_deadline_note: Round 2 closes 6 January 2027, round 3 on 10 March 2027, round 4 on 28 April 2027.
courses.notes: 2027 overseas fee is shown as 'Not set'; GBP 46,000 is the 2026-27 guide figure, so target year fee not yet published. English language level not stated on any Computing page opened. The department page says admissions for September 2027 entry open in October, which conflicts with the October 2027 start on the study page; confirm the intake date. The 75% Pakistan figure is a general postgraduate minimum.

courses.title: Mechanical Engineering
courses.duration_text: 4 or 5 years, as listed on the course page (study options include a year abroad or year in industry)
courses.overview: An integrated Masters in mechanical engineering covering solid mechanics, thermofluids, mechatronics, materials selection and manufacturing, with CAD and a group design project, ending with an individual research project.
courses.academic_requirements: Minimum entry standard A*A*A or A*AAA at A-level, or 40 points in the International Baccalaureate. Applicants must sit the Engineering and Science Admissions Test (ESAT) for 2027 entry. An ATAS certificate is needed unless from an exempt nationality.
courses.english_requirements: Not stated on the course page. Imperial's English language page lists a standard level (IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, 6.0 in every element) and a higher level (7.0 overall, 6.5 in every element) and says course pages state which applies; this one does not.
courses.career_notes: The page says graduates work across sectors including aeronautics and space and lists typical job titles, employers and further study options.
courses.application_deadline_note: UCAS deadline Wednesday 13 January 2027 at 18.00 UK time.
courses.notes: 2027 Overseas fee is 'Not set'; GBP 45,500 is the stated 2026-27 guide figure, so target year fee not yet published. No Pakistani qualification equivalence is published for undergraduate entry (accepted qualifications page does not list Pakistan). English language level not stated on the course page.

courses.title: Aeronautical Engineering
courses.duration_text: 4 years (5 years with a year abroad or year in industry)
courses.overview: An integrated Masters covering aerodynamics, lightweight structures, structural mechanics, flight mechanics, mechatronics, propulsion and turbomachinery, with a group design project in year three.
courses.academic_requirements: Minimum entry standard A*A*A or A*AAA at A-level, or 40 points in the International Baccalaureate. Applicants must sit the Engineering and Science Admissions Test (ESAT) for 2027 entry.
courses.english_requirements: Not stated on the course page. Imperial's English language page lists a standard level (IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, 6.0 in every element) and a higher level (7.0 overall, 6.5 in every element) and says course pages state which applies; this one does not.
courses.career_notes: The page lists roles such as Aerospace Engineer, Graduate Engineer, Robotics Engineer and Data Analyst, and reports 98% of graduates in highly skilled work or further study (2023-24 data).
courses.application_deadline_note: UCAS deadline Wednesday 13 January 2027 at 18.00 UK time.
courses.notes: 2027 Overseas fee is 'Not set'; GBP 45,500 is the stated 2026-27 guide figure, so target year fee not yet published. No Pakistani qualification equivalence is published for undergraduate entry. English language level not stated on the course page.

scholarships.name: Imperial Inspires Scholarship (Undergraduate)
scholarships.value_text: GBP 15,000 for each year of the course (150 awards)
scholarships.summary: A tuition scholarship for new international undergraduates paying the Overseas fee rate, on full-time on-campus courses in the Faculties of Engineering, Natural Sciences and Medicine and Imperial Business School. Eligible applicants are invited to apply after submitting their UCAS application.
scholarships.criteria_text: Overseas fee status, new entrant, full-time on-campus course in a listed faculty, minimum entry requirements met and an invitation to apply. No nationality list is published and financial need is not mentioned.
scholarships.deadline_note: UCAS application by 13 January 2027 (15 October 2026 for MBBS); scholarship application by 23:59 UK time on 5 February 2027; outcome by 30 April 2027. Applications open in October 2026, date to be confirmed.
scholarships.notes: The page does not say whether an offer is needed before applying, and does not name Pakistan; eligibility rests on Overseas fee status.

scholarships.name: Imperial Inspires Scholarship (Postgraduate Taught)
scholarships.summary: A tuition scholarship for new full-time international postgraduate taught and Masters research students paying the Overseas fee rate, in listed departments across Engineering, Natural Sciences, Medicine and Imperial Business School. Applicants meeting minimum requirements are invited to apply.
scholarships.criteria_text: Overseas fee status, new entrant, full-time study in a listed department; invited to apply after meeting minimum entry requirements, with two weeks from the invitation to complete the form. No written task required.
scholarships.deadline_note: No date on the scholarship page; the deadline varies by department and application round.
scholarships.notes: The page does not name Pakistan, say whether an offer is needed first, or give an opening date. The Imperial Business School MiM page says Imperial Inspires is open to Overseas fee-paying candidates with an invitation from September 2026.

scholarships.name: Department of Aeronautics MSc Scholarship
scholarships.provider_name: Imperial College London, Department of Aeronautics
scholarships.value_text: Full tuition fees, home or overseas rate (2 awards)
scholarships.summary: A full tuition award for new entrants to selected Department of Aeronautics MSc programmes. A complete application to an eligible course is considered automatically, with no separate scholarship form.
scholarships.criteria_text: Complete application to MSc Advanced Aeronautical Engineering, MSc Advanced Computational Methods for Aeronautics, Flow Management and Fluid-Structure Interaction, or MSc Composites by the deadline. New entrants only; no academic criteria listed.
scholarships.notes: Page says fee status 'home or overseas' with no nationality restriction and does not mention Pakistan. Whether an offer is needed is not stated.

scholarships.name: Alex Fortescue PhD Scholarship
scholarships.provider_name: Imperial College London, Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering
scholarships.value_text: Full tuition fees at the Home or Overseas rate plus a UKRI London rate stipend for 3.5 years (1 award)
scholarships.summary: A studentship for one new PhD student in Electrical and Electronic Engineering, with a project in Human and Artificial Intelligence topics. Applicants of any nationality may be considered and are nominated by a supervisor after receiving a PhD offer.
scholarships.criteria_text: PhD application to the department by the deadline; a PhD offer is needed for nomination by a supervisor; project must align with Human and Artificial Intelligence and related research areas; new entrants only.
scholarships.deadline_note: The date is the PhD application deadline to the department.
scholarships.notes: The page does not give the stipend amount or say whether a Pakistani applicant would be assessed at Home or Overseas rate.

scholarships.name: Imperial Business School Dean's Impact Scholarship (MSc Management)
scholarships.value_text: GBP 25,000 reduction of the MSc Management tuition fee
scholarships.summary: A tuition reduction for MSc in Management applicants with an excellent academic record and demonstrable impact in entrepreneurship, technology, sustainability, social impact or leadership. Applicants complete a written assessment after applying to the programme.
scholarships.criteria_text: Excellent academic record and demonstrable impact in entrepreneurship, technology, sustainability, social impact or leadership.
scholarships.deadline_note: No scholarship deadline stated; apply early as awards may not be given in every round.
scholarships.notes: Page does not name Pakistan or restrict by nationality. The larger award replaces a smaller one; no Business School scholarship if another award already pays full tuition.

scholarships.name: Imperial Business School MiM Future Leaders Scholarship
scholarships.value_text: GBP 20,000 reduction of the MSc Management tuition fee
scholarships.summary: A tuition reduction for MSc in Management candidates with leadership qualities, a clear career plan and the ability to inspire others. Applicants complete a written assessment after applying to the programme.
scholarships.criteria_text: MSc Management candidates with leadership qualities, a clear career plan and the ability to inspire others.
scholarships.deadline_note: No scholarship deadline stated; apply early as awards may not be given in every round.
scholarships.notes: Page does not name Pakistan or restrict by nationality.

scholarships.name: Imperial Excellence Scholarship (MSc Management)
scholarships.value_text: Up to GBP 15,000 reduction of the MSc Management tuition fee
scholarships.summary: A merit-based tuition reduction for top MSc in Management candidates, assessed through the application and interview. Eligible applicants who receive an offer are considered automatically.
scholarships.criteria_text: Top merit-based candidates, assessed through application and interview.
scholarships.notes: Exact award value within the 'up to' amount is not published.

scholarships.name: Imperial Alumni Discount (MSc Management)
scholarships.value_text: 10% of tuition (GBP 5,100) off the MSc Management fee
scholarships.summary: A 10% tuition discount for Imperial College London alumni joining the MSc in Management. It is applied automatically with an offer.
scholarships.notes: Stated on the MiM page only; other Business School Masters pages were not checked for an equivalent discount.
